**The Weight of Empty Spaces**

I woke up to the sound of rain tapping against the window like an old man’s cane—slow, deliberate, testing the floorboards. The room was too quiet, the kind of quiet that hums in your bones. I lay there for a while, listening to the rhythm of the drops, wondering if the world was holding its breath or if it had already exhaled and forgotten to inhale again.

Outside, the streetlights bled into the wet pavement, turning the asphalt into a mirror of fractured light. A car passed, its headlights slicing through the gloom, and for a second, I saw my reflection in the glass—pale, hollow-eyed, a stranger wearing my face. I wondered if anyone else noticed how easily we become ghosts in our own lives.

I got up and made coffee, the bitter smell filling the kitchen like a warning. The clock on the wall ticked too loudly, each second stretching like taffy. I thought about calling someone—anyone—but the words stuck in my throat. What would I say? *Hello, it’s me. I’m still here, but barely.* Or maybe, *I don’t know how to be alive today.* Either way, it felt like too much effort.

Instead, I sat by the window and watched the rain. It was one of those days where the world felt too big and too small at the same time. Too big because there were so many people out there living, laughing, loving, while I sat in the quiet of my own absence. Too small because in the grand scheme of things, my little sorrows were just noise in the static.

I thought about the last time I felt truly alive. It wasn’t a grand moment—no epiphany, no revelation. Just a Tuesday, maybe, when I laughed so hard my stomach hurt. Or the way the sun felt on my skin after weeks of gray. Those moments were fleeting, like fireflies in a jar. You try to hold onto them, but the jar always cracks, and the light escapes.

I wondered if happiness was just the absence of pain, or if pain was the absence of something else entirely. Maybe we’re all just walking around with these holes inside us, trying to fill them with noise and work and relationships, but the holes are too big, and no matter how much we stuff in, it never quite fits.

The rain stopped. The world outside looked washed clean, like it had been scrubbed raw. I thought about going for a walk, but my legs felt heavy, as if the air itself was pressing down on me. So I stayed. And for a while, that was enough.

---

**The Things We Carry**

I’ve been thinking about luggage lately. Not the kind you pack for a trip, but the kind we drag around without realizing it. The weight of old arguments, the suitcase of regrets, the backpack of things we wish we’d said.

There’s a story about a man who carried a boulder in his arms every day. People asked why, and he said, *"It’s my burden to bear."* One day, he set it down and walked away. When they asked how he could leave it, he said, *"I was always the one carrying it. The boulder never asked me to."*

We do that, don’t we? We pick up things we don’t need and then act surprised when they slow us down. A harsh word from years ago, a missed opportunity, a love that slipped through our fingers. We tuck them into our pockets and forget they’re there until the weight becomes unbearable.

I wonder what would happen if we just… put some of it down. Not because we’re weak, but because we’re tired. Because holding on isn’t the same as being strong. Sometimes, strength is knowing when to let go.

---

**The Language of Silence**

There are moments when words fail. Not because we don’t have anything to say, but because what needs to be said can’t be spoken—only felt. A glance across a crowded room. The way someone’s hands tremble when they’re trying not to cry. The silence between two people who understand each other without a single word.

I’ve always been bad at small talk. I’d rather sit in the quiet with someone than fill the air with noise that means nothing. But silence can be a kind of language too. It can say, *I’m here. I see you. You don’t have to pretend.*

Maybe that’s why I write. Not to fill the silence, but to make it speak.

---

**The Art of Disappearing**

There’s a quiet kind of magic in fading into the background. Not in a sad way, but in the way a shadow fades when the light moves. You become part of the scenery, just another face in the crowd, another voice in the hum of the world.

I’ve always envied people who can do that effortlessly. The ones who walk into a room and no one notices, and then, just as quietly, they leave. No fuss, no drama. Just… gone.

But then I think about the people who can’t disappear. The ones who are always *on*, always performing, always performing for an audience that may not even be there. The ones who are afraid of being forgotten, so they shout to be heard.

Maybe the trick isn’t to disappear or to be seen, but to find the balance. To be present without demanding attention. To love without needing to be loved back in the same way.

---

**The Last Thought Before Sleep**

Tonight, as I lie in bed, I wonder what tomorrow will bring. Not in a grand, life-changing way, but in the small, quiet ways that make up a day. The first sip of coffee. The way the light hits the wall at a certain angle. The sound of a neighbor’s laughter drifting through the window.

I used to think that happiness was something I had to chase, like a horizon that kept moving further away. But maybe it’s not out there at all. Maybe it’s in the way the rain sounds on the roof. In the way my cat curls up against my side. In the quiet moments when the world feels soft and still.

I close my eyes and let the darkness hold me. For now, that’s enough.
